definitions.explanation: Lacking courtesy or respect. A somewhat formal or literary way of describing rude behavior.

examples.japanese: {無礼|ぶれい}な{態度|たいど}をとった。
{無礼|ぶれい}を{承知|しょうち}で{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: I say this knowing it may be rude.
examples.notes: A set phrase used before saying something potentially offensive.

examples.japanese: {目上|めうえ}の{人|ひと}に{対|たい}して{無礼|ぶれい}な{言葉|ことば}を{使|つか}うのは{許|ゆる}されない。
examples.english: Using disrespectful language toward a superior is unacceptable.

notes:
USAGE: More formal and literary than {失礼|しつれい} (rude, impolite). {無礼|ぶれい} carries a stronger, more serious tone and implies a deeper breach of social etiquette.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無礼|ぶれい}な{態度|たいど}: rude attitude
- {無礼|ぶれい}な{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}い: rude behavior
- {無礼|ぶれい}を{働|はたら}く: to behave rudely
- {無礼|ぶれい}を{承知|しょうち}で: knowing it may be rude
- {無礼|ぶれい}{講|こう}: a drinking party where rank is set aside

CONTRAST: {無礼|ぶれい} (rude, stronger) vs. {失礼|しつれい} (impolite, milder/everyday).
